whatWasActuallyWrong.carriedFinding: VF03 rows-vf03-20260909c.json repairsNeeded, and MASTER_QUEUE.json failedObligations[0] for this family: 146 dangling indirect references per fixture; trailer /Size 954 against a cross-reference table covering 808 object numbers in 14 subsections; Poppler refusing both fixtures with 'Syntax Error: Couldn't find trailer dictionary'.
whatWasActuallyWrong.reproducedAtBase: TRUE, measured rather than accepted. At base 0cb08c3617e4d54223f581a9f3a8a17894d3f93e the control read canonical and boundary at danglingAnnots 146, resolvedAnnots 21 (all 21 Link), trailerSize 954, xrefCovered 808, xrefSubsections 14, xrefUncovered 146. pdfinfo on the base canonical printed 'Syntax Error: Couldn't find trailer dictionary', then 'Invalid XRef entry 8', 'Invalid XRef entry 9', 'Invalid XRef entry 10' -- the exact three objects page object 80's /Annots names and the file does not contain.
whatWasActuallyWrong.mechanism: pdf-lib's form.flatten() deletes the widget annotation objects from the document context and leaves their indirect references in each page's /Annots array. buildPacket then copies those pages into a fresh packet document, and PDFObjectCopier reserves a fresh object number for each unresolvable reference and never emits an object at it. That is why the two symptoms carry the SAME number: each dangling reference consumes exactly one reserved-and-never-written object number, so 954 - 808 = 146 = the dangling count, and the writer emits one xref subsection per surviving run of real objects, which is where the 14 subsections come from.
whatWasActuallyWrong.whyItPredatesFIX118: The defect is in the flatten-then-copy path, which FIX118 did not touch. Consistent with VF03's confirmation at 159c0b5cf, and with the fact that il-exp-pardon-set and il-seal-edu-set -- which have called the same prune since they were written -- ship clean.

verifiersProposedRepairEvaluatedNotAdopt.proposed: After form.flatten(), prune each page's /Annots of unresolvable references (Link annots resolve and must stay), AND emit an xref covering 0..Size-1 with unused numbers marked free.
verifiersProposedRepairEvaluatedNotAdopt.firstHalfAdopted: Yes, and moved earlier than 'after form.flatten()' would suggest on its own: the prune runs on each COMPONENT document immediately after flatten, before copyPages, because copyPages is what converts a surviving dangling reference into a reserved object number. A second prune runs on the merged packet as a guard; on a correctly pruned component set it removes nothing.
verifiersProposedRepairEvaluatedNotAdopt.secondHalfRejectedWithEvidence: No free-entry xref pass was written, because pruning at the component document makes it unnecessary rather than merely redundant. With no dangling reference to copy, no object number is reserved-and-never-written, pdf-lib's /Size falls to the true largest object number and the writer emits a SINGLE full-coverage subsection on its own. Measured after repair: trailerSize 808, xrefCovered 808, xrefSubsections 1, xrefUncovered 0 -- identical in shape to the already-clean il-exp-pardon-set and il-seal-edu-set. Hand-emitting an xref would have been a second, unverified PDF writer sitting downstream of pdf-lib's, and it would have masked rather than removed the cause.
